text: Ragged stunt (locally ជំងឺតឿរួញស្លឹក) is another brown-planthopper-transmitted rice disease, distinct from grassy stunt though sharing the same vector. Infected plants are stunted from an early growth stage; leaves are short, dark green, and have a ragged, torn, or notched appearance along the margins, with blades that look twisted or curled rather than lying flat. Leaf sheaths and the flag leaf are similarly shortened and twisted, and the jagged, torn leaf-margin appearance along the veins is the most distinctive visual sign separating this disease from grassy stunt. The practical impact is that infected plants either fail to head properly or produce only partial, incomplete panicle emergence. As with grassy stunt, risk rises with the size of the nearby brown planthopper population and with the availability of infected source plants nearby. Recommended control: use resistant varieties where available; apply balanced fertilizer and avoid excess nitrogen; remove and destroy infected plants found in the field; and directly monitor and control the brown planthopper vector population through integrated planthopper management. This is a confirmed new addition to the disease knowledge base, closing part of the previously identified gap in confirmed virus/planthopper-vectored rice disease coverage.
